claims.explanation: The selective killing pattern is best explained by estrogen receptor (ESR1) signaling: lines with high ESR1 expression or estrogen-responsive transcriptional programs are sensitized to the ER agonist estradiol cypionate, while those with low ESR1 or mutations in core estrogen signaling components are protected. The enrichment of TP53 mutations in sensitive lines suggests that intact p53 may mediate a protective response to estrogen-induced stress, and its loss sensitizes cells. Other features such as PTEN loss and MAPK pathway mutations may further modulate sensitivity through cross-talk with ER signaling.

features.basis: Drug is an ER agonist; high ESR1 expression predicts response to estrogen receptor agonists.
Observed pattern: TP53 mutations are highly enriched in sensitive lines, suggesting loss of p53-mediated protective response.
Observed pattern: PTEN mutations appear in several sensitive lines; PTEN loss may enhance ER signaling.
Observed pattern: MAP2K1 mutation in sensitive line NCIH1437; MAPK activation may sensitize to estrogen.
Observed pattern: BRAF mutations in sensitive melanoma lines; BRAF V600E may interact with ER signaling.
Observed pattern: KRAS mutations in sensitive pancreatic lines; KRAS-driven tumors may depend on ER signaling.
Observed pattern: NF1 mutations in several sensitive lines; NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK, potentially sensitizing.
Observed pattern: EGFR mutations appear in both sensitive and resistant lines, but some resistant lines have EGFR mutations; may confer resistance.
Observed pattern: CDKN2A mutations appear in resistant lines; loss may protect through cell cycle deregulation.
Observed pattern: ARID1A mutations are enriched in resistant lines; chromatin remodeling defects may reduce ER dependence.
Observed pattern: KMT2D mutations appear in resistant lines; may alter estrogen-responsive enhancer landscapes.
Observed pattern: PIK3CA mutations appear in resistant lines; PI3K activation may bypass ER dependence.
